blocks.html: What JUPEB is

JUPEB (Joint Universities Preliminary Examinations Board) runs an A-Level standard programme recognised by Nigerian universities. Students who succeed can use their JUPEB results to apply for Direct Entry admission into 200 Level, skipping the first year of a degree. At BIA the programme runs for 8–9 months, with physical classes near the University of Lagos and online lessons for students who cannot attend in person.
Who the programme is for

items: O’Level holders aiming for 200 Level. You can register with your O’Level result — or with an awaiting result (see our awaiting-result guide).
Students who learn online. If you cannot attend physical classes, the Lecture Banks carry the teaching, materials and guidance you need.
Students from other institutions. You can join BIA’s physical tutorials only, through the Physical Tutorial Services Package.

blocks.html: What you need to register
BIA’s 2026/27 payment advice lists four requirements:

items: The full registration fee — ₦45,000 for the application form (compulsory).
Your O’Level result. If it is not out yet, an awaiting result is acceptable.
Your National Identification Number (NIN).
Your birth certificate.

blocks.html: All payments to BIA are final and non-refundable once processed. Be certain before you pay, and keep every payment receipt safe — you will need them for record and verification purposes.

How the 2026/27 year runs

items: Registration. Pay the registration fee and submit your documents. The first instalment of the programme fee is paid on registration and closes before the BIA Entrance Examination.

BIA Entrance Examination. This exam is not used to refuse anyone admission. It assesses each student’s strengths and the areas to improve before the programme starts. Students who do not perform well are still admitted, but may be advised or required to take additional academic support.

Free Special Marathon Class. A free academic support class held before the main physical resumption to strengthen your foundation. For 2026/27 it ran from 5 to 31 October 2026, alongside free online tutorials.
Resumption and First Semester. The second instalment is due upon resumption — by January, before the First Semester Examination or the final JUPEB biometrics.
Final JUPEB thumbprint and biometrics exercise. BIA’s payment schedule is tied to this exercise; the admissions office confirms its date.
Second Semester. The fee balance is due on or before 4 May 2027, before Second Semester resumption.
Direct Entry. After your JUPEB results, BIA guides you through the Direct Entry window, timelines and documentation — see JUPEB to UNILAG.

blocks.html: Two rhythms run on top of the weekly timetable: every third week, night classes are held as intensive preparation for the monthly mock, and every fourth week the Monthly Mock Examination takes place at the end of the week. Treat the Saturday tests and the mocks as checkpoints — they show you which topics need attention while there is still time to fix them.

SFS on the timetable refers to the University of Lagos School of Foundation Studies, which runs UNILAG’s own JUPEB programme. BIA’s first-semester timetable is for BIA private JUPEB students and some selected UNILAG School of Foundation students. Subject codes, “001” and “002” are shown as printed on BIA’s timetable.
Choosing your subjects
Your JUPEB subject combination must match the course you want to study at university. Some common examples:

items: Medicine: Biology, Chemistry, Physics
Law: Literature-in-English, Government, Christian Religious Studies
Engineering: Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry

blocks.html: All three combinations appear in the list of JUPEB subject combinations offered by UNILAG’s School of Foundation Studies (2025/26 admission notice). Which combination suits which degree is BIA’s advice — confirm yours with the admissions office.

Decide your target course first, then choose subjects — not the other way round. Before you register, check the Direct Entry requirements for that course at the university you want, and ask the admissions office to confirm your combination.
How to register

items: Call or WhatsApp the admissions office on 0701 238 8184, or visit BIA (addresses on the contact page).
Bring your documents: O’Level result (or awaiting result), NIN and birth certificate.
Pay the ₦45,000 registration fee and keep the receipt.
Confirm your subject combination and study option with the admissions office.
Sit the BIA Entrance Examination and follow any academic support you are advised to take.

blocks.html: Registration is handled by the admissions office — it is not done through this website.
Frequently asked questions
Can I do the whole programme online?
Yes. Students who cannot attend physical classes, or who prefer online learning, study through the Lecture Banks, which BIA makes compulsory for them.
Can a poor Entrance Examination result stop me being admitted?
No. The Entrance Examination identifies where you need help. Students who do not perform well are still admitted, but may be advised or required to take extra academic support.
Is the registration fee refundable?
No. All payments are final and non-refundable once processed, so be certain before you pay.
Can I pay the programme fee in parts?
Yes — in three instalments: on registration, on resumption, and the balance on or before 4 May 2027. The admissions office confirms each amount; see the fees page.

blocks.html: Why this guide focuses on UNILAG

BIA’s admission guidance currently focuses on the University of Lagos (UNILAG), and BIA’s tutorial centre is in Akoka, near UNILAG. Of the university placements BIA has recorded on this website, the large majority are at UNILAG; the rest include Osun State University and Mercy Medical University.

Step 1: Choose subjects that fit your course

UNILAG considers your JUPEB subjects when you apply, so your combination must match your intended course. For example, Medicine uses Biology, Chemistry and Physics; Law uses Literature-in-English, Government and Christian Religious Studies; Engineering uses Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry.

External check: each of these three combinations is on the list of JUPEB combinations offered by UNILAG’s School of Foundation Studies (2025/26 notice). The notice lists combinations but not the degree each one leads to; that matching is BIA’s guidance.

If you are deciding between two courses — say Medicine and Pharmacy — choose a combination that keeps both open, and confirm it with the admissions office before you register. More on choosing subjects is in the JUPEB guide.
Step 2: Understand how your grades become points
Each JUPEB grade converts to points:
Why results are out of 16
JUPEB results are reported as a total out of 16 points. The University of Lagos describes 16 as “the highest grade attainable” (UNILAG, December 2025).
From BIA’s records: in every result BIA has published with grade letters, the total is the three grade points plus one:
BIA’s records do not state the rule behind the additional point, so this guide does not explain it. If your result or a course requirement depends on it, ask the admissions office.

UNILAG is competitive, and courses such as Medicine need high points. The practical lesson: one weak subject can pull your total down more than you expect, so do not neglect the subject you find hardest. Use BIA’s Saturday tests and monthly mocks to find that subject early.
Step 3: Use the assessment rhythm

items: Saturday tests every week show you where you stand in each subject.
Night classes every third week prepare you for the mock.
The Monthly Mock Examination, every fourth week, is your best rehearsal for the real exam.

blocks.html: After each test, write down the topics you lost marks on and revisit them before the next one. Students who track their mistakes this way see the same weak topics come up again — and fix them.
Step 4: Keep your documents in order
Start a folder on day one and keep it up to date:

items: O’Level result (bring it to the admissions office as soon as it is released if you registered while awaiting)
National Identification Number (NIN) and birth certificate
Every BIA payment receipt — BIA asks students to keep them for record and verification
Your JUPEB admission letter
Your JUPEB result, once released

blocks.html: Step 5: Apply for Direct Entry in the approved window

After JUPEB, apply for UNILAG Direct Entry within the approved application window. BIA guides you on the timelines and the documents required. Keep your results and admission documents ready and continue preparing academically: UNILAG may ask for additional screening or verification.

What UNILAG says: successful JUPEB candidates “are eligible for consideration for Direct Entry admission into the 200 Level of the Degree Programmes of the University through JAMB (Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board)”, and “success at JUPEB examination does not always translate into admission for preferred course of choice” (UNILAG, 2025/26).

For 2025/26 registration, UNILAG asked newly admitted Direct Entry candidates for documents including the UNILAG online application form, JAMB acknowledgement slip, JAMB admission letter, O’Level result certificate and JUPEB result slip (UNILAG registration notice). Check the notice for your own year — the list can change.
Frequently asked questions
Does BIA only help with UNILAG?
BIA’s guidance currently focuses on UNILAG. Its records also include students placed at other universities, including Osun State University and Mercy Medical University.
How many points do I need for my course at UNILAG?
Requirements differ by course and can change each year, so this guide does not list them. Ask the admissions office about the course you are aiming for before you choose your subjects.
I study online — does BIA still guide me on Direct Entry?
Online students follow the JUPEB programme through the Lecture Banks. Ask the admissions office how Direct Entry guidance works for online students in your session.

metaTitle: JUPEB vs IJMB: Which Should You Choose in 2026? | BIA JUPEB
description: JUPEB and IJMB compared for Direct Entry: duration, grading and study options, plus the questions to answer before you choose one.
title: JUPEB vs IJMB: which should you choose?
lead: Both lead to Direct Entry into 200 Level. The right choice depends less on which is “easier” and more on your target university, your timeline and how you study.
sources: V1 biajupeb.com.ng text (BIA’s own): JUPEB 8–9 months, IJMB 9–12 months depending on centre; both accepted by many Nigerian universities; similar grading, calendar and format may differ; UNILAG focus
BIA Payment Advice 2026/27: Lecture Banks notice, payment stages
BIA JUPEB First Semester Timetable, 2026/27

blocks.html: The short answer

Neither programme is easier for everyone. Both are accepted by many Nigerian universities for Direct Entry into 200 Level. JUPEB is usually shorter, which saves time; IJMB is usually longer, which some students use for extra revision. Choose the one your target university accepts for your course, that fits your timeline, and that you can commit to fully.
Side by side

blocks.caption: JUPEB and IJMB at a glance
head: JUPEB
IJMB
rows: Usually longer — up to about 12 months. Check the exact length with the study centre
Letter grades converted to points (A = 5 down to E = 1); results reported out of 16

blocks.html: “Accepted by many universities” is not the same as “accepted by yours, for your course”. Always check the Direct Entry requirements of the university and course you want before you commit.
Five questions to answer before you choose

items: Which university and course do I want? Check that it accepts the programme for Direct Entry into that course.
When do I want to be in 200 Level? A shorter programme gets you there sooner if you are ready for the pace.
Can I attend in person? If not, look for a programme with proper online teaching — at BIA, the Lecture Banks.
Do I work well with regular testing? BIA’s JUPEB programme has tests every Saturday and a mock examination every fourth week.
Can I meet the payment schedule? At BIA the programme fee is paid in three stages across the session — see the fees page.

blocks.html: Why the shorter programme suits many students

A shorter programme means less time between leaving secondary school and starting 200 Level, and fewer months of fees and living costs. The trade-off is pace: there is less slack if you fall behind. That is why steady habits matter more than raw ability — attending consistently, taking every Saturday test seriously and fixing weak topics before the monthly mock.
JUPEB at BIA in brief

BIA prepares Science and Non-Science students for JUPEB over 8–9 months, with physical classes near UNILAG, online Lecture Banks, weekly tests and monthly mocks, and admission guidance focused on the University of Lagos. The JUPEB guide explains how the year runs.
Frequently asked questions
Is JUPEB accepted at UNILAG?
BIA’s admission guidance focuses on UNILAG, and most of the university placements BIA has recorded for its JUPEB students are at UNILAG — see JUPEB to UNILAG.
Which is cheaper?
Costs depend on the centre. BIA’s JUPEB fees for 2026/27 are on the fees page; compare them with the full cost of any other option, including how long you will be studying.
Which has the harder exams?
Students find different things hard. What makes the biggest difference is preparation: regular practice, honest review of mistakes and using mock examinations as rehearsals.

blocks.html: The short answer: yes
BIA’s 2026/27 requirements say it plainly: bring your O’Level result — if not available, awaiting results is acceptable. You can register and start preparing before your result is released.
Your O’Level requirements must be complete before final JUPEB registration closes. The admissions office will tell you the timeline for your session.
What to bring when you register

blocks.caption: Registration checklist
head: Item
Notes
rows: ₦45,000 for the application form. Compulsory and non-refundable — keep the receipt.
An awaiting result is acceptable at registration.

blocks.html: Using the waiting time well
Waiting for a result is not wasted time. Students who register early get the most out of BIA’s preparation:

items: Sit the BIA Entrance Examination. It does not decide whether you are admitted — it shows your strengths and the areas to work on before the programme starts.

Join the free preparation before resumption. In 2026/27, BIA ran a free Special Marathon Class from 5 to 31 October, with free online tutorials, to strengthen students’ foundations before the main physical resumption.
Practise. BIA’s CBT practice platform has JUPEB and JAMB-style questions with instant grading.
Get your documents ready. Make sure you have your NIN and birth certificate to hand, so the only thing outstanding is your result.

blocks.html: The day your result is released

items: Print or save a copy of your result.
Bring it to the BIA admissions office straight away — delays can hold up your final JUPEB registration.
Check that your name is written the same way on your result, NIN and birth certificate. If anything differs, tell the admissions office immediately.
Keep a copy in the same folder as your payment receipts.

blocks.html: If your result is not what you hoped
Speak to the admissions office as soon as possible — before making any further payment. BIA’s payments are final and non-refundable, so get clear advice on your situation first.
Frequently asked questions
Will I be refused if I do badly in the Entrance Examination?
No. Students who do not perform well are still admitted, but may be advised or required to take additional academic support.
Do I get my registration fee back if my result is delayed?
No — all payments are final and non-refundable once processed. That is why it pays to register early and keep in touch with the admissions office.
Can I start classes before my result is out?
Awaiting results are accepted at registration, so you can register and begin preparing. The admissions office will tell you when your result must be submitted.

blocks.html: How BIA students get past questions

BIA provides past questions directly to registered students, across Science, Arts and Commercial subjects. They are not sold through this website. If you have not registered yet, start with the JUPEB guide and contact the admissions office.

When

blocks.html: The CBT practice platform lets you choose how you log in — free class or paying tutorial — and shows your score as soon as you submit.
A routine for using past questions

items: Learn the topic first. Attempt questions on a topic after it has been taught, not before — otherwise you are guessing, not practising.
Start untimed, by topic. Work through questions one topic at a time and check every answer, including the ones you got right by luck.
Keep an error log. For every wrong answer, write the topic, what went wrong (didn’t know it, misread it, ran out of time) and the correct method.
Repeat after a week. Redo the questions you got wrong without looking at your notes. If you still get them wrong, the topic needs reteaching — take it to your tutor.
Move to timed papers. Once topics are solid, do full papers under time pressure so the mock and the real exam feel familiar.
Review after every test and mock. Add new mistakes to your log. The same weak topics tend to reappear — that is your revision list.

blocks.html: Fitting it into the BIA week
The first-semester timetable already gives you the structure:

items: Monday and Wednesday are self-study and lecture days — use part of them for topic practice on what was taught that week.
Tuesday and Thursday are class days — note anything you did not follow and check it against past questions that evening.
Saturday is test day — afterwards, update your error log.
Before each monthly mock, use the third-week night classes and your error log to target your weakest topics.

blocks.html: Common mistakes to avoid

items: Memorising answers instead of understanding the method — the same idea is often asked in a different way.
Practising only your favourite subject. Every subject counts towards your result.
Never practising under time pressure, then running out of time in the exam.
Skipping the review. Doing questions without checking why you got them wrong teaches very little.

blocks.html: Frequently asked questions
Can I get BIA’s past questions before I register?
BIA currently provides past questions directly to registered students. Complete your registration first, then ask the team for access.
Which subjects are covered?
BIA supports Science, Arts and Commercial subjects. Ask the admissions office about the papers available for your combination.
How do I log in to the CBT platform?
Open the platform and choose how you log in — free class or paying tutorial — then enter your details and start a test. Call admissions on 0701 238 8184 if you have trouble logging in.
